paragraphs.source_en: All the main Central Saharan mountainous massifs present prehistoric rock art. In the Tassili n'Ajjer, Algerian Tadrart and Tadrart Acacus both paintings and engravings are present and the Round Head paintings therefore coexist with other forms of rock art. However, the term coexistence is referring to a vast territory because only in exceptional cases do we find Round Head paintings and prehistoric engravings in the same shelter. The division of territories for different artistic expressions, namely the paintings and engravings, may have been caused by different periods of creation or by different cultures.

paragraphs.source_en: Although it has been studied for more than five decades, the chronology and categorization of the Central Saharan rock art remain the subject of great controversy. Thus, it is still not certain if the earliest paintings and engravings are to be placed in the Late Pleistocene or into the Early or even the Middle Holocene. According to artistic groups determined by various criteria, such as the technique of production, patina on the art, anthropological type, the fauna represented, themes, superimpositions and style; a classification was set up by previous scholars (e. g. Lhote 1958, 1976; Mori 1971). Saharan engravings and paintings were divided into several distinct large groups, lasting for variable periods. The proposed styles would function not only as a classificatory scheme but also as a sequence of relative chronology, with each class being granted the status of a period.

paragraphs.source_en: This chronological-stylistic sequence is still widely used by many researchers, however, it has become a target for criticism in recent decades (Muzzolini 1996; Hachid 1998; Jelinek 2004). The lack of direct dating gives a wide margin for subjective chronological interpretation, resulting in two chronologies being established, a high (earlier) and a low (later) one. Whilst the high chronology places the oldest engravings to the Pleistocene period (Mori 2000), the low one does not accept any form of rock art being made before the Holocene period (Muzzolini 1995a, Le Quellec 2006b).
